AK-senate.statusNote: Sen. Dan Sullivan (R) and Mary Peltola (D) advanced from the Aug 18 top-four primary to the November ranked choice general, along with Dan J. Sullivan of Petersburg (R). The fourth spot is still open: in the state's Aug 26 count update, David Leslie (D) led Gerald Heikes (R) by 43 votes, with absentee ballots accepted through Aug 28 and certification expected Aug 31.

AK-governor.statusNote: Open seat: Gov. Mike Dunleavy is term-limited and cannot seek a third consecutive term. In the Aug 18 top-four primary, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D), who represented Sitka and Southeast Alaska in the Legislature for a decade, and former Anchorage state Sen. Tom Begich (D) lead with about 22% and 20%. Conservative activist and business owner Bernadette Wilson (R) holds third at about 10%. The fourth spot is not settled: former Anchorage Mayor Dave Bronson (R) leads a tight pack, with certification expected Aug 31. The November general uses ranked choice voting. Positions are not researched yet.

AK-house-at-large.statusNote: Rep. Nick Begich III (R) and independent Bill Hill, a commercial fisherman and retired educator, advanced from the Aug 18 top-four primary. Democrat Eric Hafner also advanced after third-place finisher Matt Schultz (D) withdrew; Hafner is serving a federal prison sentence until 2036, has no clear ties to Alaska, and legal challenges to his candidacy are expected. The final spot is not settled, with certification expected Aug 31. The November general uses ranked choice voting. Positions are not researched yet.

candidates.name: Dan Sullivan
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 2015; retired 30-year Marine Corps officer. Previously Alaska Attorney General, state Natural Resources Commissioner, and an Assistant Secretary of State. Seeking a third term.

cost.label: Frames affordability through tax relief and resource development; claims the 2025 tax bill raises family take-home pay (Senate office)

health.label: Opposed the ACA and voted to repeal it (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Introduced the bipartisan Workforce Housing Tax Credit Act to build middle-income housing; calls Alaska's housing crisis 'a top priority' (Senate office)

immigration.label: Border-security-first: touts the $46B border security funding in the 2025 bill (Senate office)

taxes.label: Champions making the 2017 tax cuts permanent; 'prevented the largest tax hike in history' (Senate office)

climate.label: 'Unleashing Alaska's energy potential': shaped the 2025 bill mandating ANWR, NPR-A, and Cook Inlet lease sales over the next decade (Senate office)

safety.label: Leads statewide 'One Pill Can Kill' anti-fentanyl campaign: interdiction with law enforcement plus prevention and treatment (Senate office)

repro.label: Opposes abortion except for rape, incest, or threat to the mother's life (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Voted against advancing the Freedom to Vote: John R. Lewis Act; cloture on H.R. 5746 failed 49-51 (Senate roll call 9, Jan 2022)

controversies.label: 2020 undercover recordings captured Pebble Mine executives suggesting he would quietly support the mine after the election; he publicly opposed it afterward (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Mary Peltola
candidates.background: Yup'ik former fishing-boat captain and the first Alaska Native elected to Congress (2022-2025); the last Democrat to win statewide in Alaska. Served 10 years in the Alaska House and led the Kuskokwim River Inter-Tribal Fish Commission. A moderate who frequently broke party ranks.
priorities: Fix the 'rigged system': term limits, anti-corruption
Restore Alaska fisheries; ban factory trawling

cost.label: Affordability plan: ban price gouging, block anti-competitive grocery mergers, expand the child tax credit, restore rural Bypass Mail (campaign site)

health.label: Supports extending ACA premium subsidies and opposed Medicaid cuts (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Would 'crack down on the out-of-state corporations and hedge funds buying up homes'; tax credits for rent-burdened renters (campaign site)

immigration.label: Mixed: broke with Democrats to back Republican-led enforcement measures, including deporting undocumented migrants who assault police (Wikipedia)

climate.label: All-of-the-above: pushed Willow approval and the Alaska LNG pipeline AND would restore federal tax credits for solar, wind, and hydro (campaign energy page)

education.label: Opposes school vouchers; 'quality schools are vital to the future of our communities' (OnTheIssues, 2022)

repro.label: Pro-choice; supports codifying Roe v. Wade protections in federal law (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Voted against H.J.Res. 26, the resolution overturning DC's revised criminal code and its lower sentences; it passed 250-173 (House roll call 119, 2023)

nullNotes.taxes: removed in QA: cited affordability page documents only targeted household tax cuts (no federal income tax under $92,000, no tax on Social Security) with no spending-cut agenda, which per calibration does not fit the axis; the 'raising taxes on the wealthiest' claim was not documented on the cited page

controversies.label: NRSC filed a 2026 FEC complaint alleging improper use of her dormant House campaign account; her campaign calls it 'a completely false attack' (Anchorage Daily News)
